title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners
layout_note: A single left-to-right strip: masked input image -> column of visible patches -> tall encoder -> column of encoded tokens -> longer column of tokens with mask tokens re-inserted -> short decoder -> column of output tokens -> full target image. The encoder box is drawn much taller than the decoder box.
grouping: No containers. The stages are separated only by short grey arrows and by the alternating shapes (token column, block, token column). Colour families group the tokens: grey for mask tokens, teal for encoded visible tokens, salmon for decoder outputs.
shapes_depth: Flat. The two networks are rounded rectangles filled light grey with a thin grey outline, labelled 'encoder' and 'decoder' in a plain sans-serif. The input and target are the same photo cut into a 5 x 5 grid by white gutters; in the input most cells are filled solid dark grey and only a few show the photo. Tokens are small square cells stacked into vertical columns with white gaps, with a vertical ellipsis standing in for the rest of a long column. The visible patches entering the encoder are shown as a column of actual photo pieces.
proposed_highlight: No highlighting of a proposed part; the design argument is made by proportion and count: a tall encoder fed by only a short column of visible patches versus a smaller decoder handling a long column that mixes grey mask tokens back in among the teal ones.
lesson: Draw the masked input as the photo cut into a grid with most cells filled flat grey, then carry the mask through the network as grey cells in the token columns, so the reader can count how few patches the encoder sees.
notes: venue as recorded by Semantic Scholar; year = arXiv preprint year (2111.06377). The input/target photos and the photo patches are embedded images excluded from the measured palette.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: one left-to-right row: masked image grid, the few visible patches, a tall encoder, short cyan token column, a long column of cyan and grey mask tokens, a small decoder, red output tokens, the reconstructed target

relations.form: eight elements in a row joined by short grey arrows, input at left and target at right
masking drawn on the real image: a 5 x 5 patch grid with most patches filled flat grey and only a few photo patches showing
the encoded cyan tokens are re-inserted among grey mask tokens in one long column before the decoder

channels.colour: grey = masked patch / mask token, cyan = encoded visible token, red = decoder output token; one meaning each
channels.shape: photo squares = patches; flat rectangles = tokens; grey rounded box = network
channels.line: short grey arrows on one axis

quality.strengths: The asymmetric design is shown by size: the encoder box is tall and sees only the visible patch column, while the decoder is small and handles the full-length column; every representation (visible patches, latent tokens, mask tokens, outputs) is drawn between the module that makes it and the one that uses it.
quality.weaknesses: The reconstruction loss between the red outputs and the target is not drawn, and the positions of the cyan tokens within the long column are not tied visibly to the grid positions of the visible patches.

insights.structure: Five-step horizontal chain: masked input grid, column of visible patches, a large grey encoder, a long token column, a smaller grey decoder, a red token column, and the target image grid.
insights.data: Images are real flamingo photos cut into a 5x5 patch grid with masked patches greyed; tokens are coloured cells in vertical columns (teal encoded, grey mask tokens, red outputs).
insights.emphasis: Size encodes the asymmetry: the encoder box is much taller than the decoder, and only the few visible patches enter the encoder while mask tokens join later.
insights.flow: Strictly left-to-right with grey arrows; vertical token columns interleave teal and grey cells to show mask tokens being inserted.

arrangement.units: unboxed chain of image grids, token columns and two rounded grey module boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: real photo with a patch-mask grid
